thread:
julie: Heads-up — multiple customers started seeing 403s after last night's API key rotation for the billing service. Not all tenants affected. Filing here to correlate.
devin: Which customers? can you paste error examples / request ids?
julie: acme-inc and brightpay reported 403s. sample req-id: r_8f3b21. Error from API gateway: "invalid_api_key". Logs show the new key is valid for some pods, but older pods still accept old key for a while.
samir: weird — we rotate keys by writing new secret to Vault, then CI triggers a rolling restart that updates envvars. Could there be a timing gap where some workers hold both keys leading to inconsistent auth caches?
julie: That's our hypothesis. Also saw vault-agent logs around the window: 
```
2026-03-15T02:11:03Z vault-agent: token renewal failed: lease expired
2026-03-15T02:11:05Z vault-agent: reauth success
```
maria: If the vault-agent lost its lease during rotation, it might not have refreshed the new secret into the pod env. Some processes may keep an in-memory cache and not pick up the updated header until restart.
kevin: Confirmed on staging — if a worker process received the new key but the auth cache persisted the old one in HTTPCache until LRU eviction, you'll have mixed behavior: some requests succeed, others 403.
devin: Repro steps I'm trying on staging: 
1) bootstrap service with key A and let workers warm caches
2) kv put secret/services/billing api_key=B (new)
3) force vault-agent reauth simulating lease bounce
4) check live requests, watch for 403 spikes

ops-bot: deploy/rotation-runner started at 2026-03-15T02:10:50Z
ops-bot: deploy/rotation-runner finished (partial) at 2026-03-15T02:12:20Z (20/30 pods updated)
samir: That partial rollout is the smoking gun. Automation didn't wait for all pods to report success. Leader-election bug in rotation-runner caused it to assume progress while some zones lagged.
julie: For immediate mitigation, can we do a coordinated full restart of the billing podset? A rolling restart will force env re-read and clear in-memory caches.
maria: I kicked a restart in us-west-2 now. Monitoring dashboards for 403s.
kevin: Quick fix script I ran on staging: 
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/billing -n prod-billing --timeout=10m
# then verify vault-agent logs for successful sync
kubectl logs -l app=billing -c vault-agent | grep "sync complete"
```
devin: For postmortem: root causes -- (1) vault-agent lease expiry during rotation, (2) rotation-runner not waiting for 100% confirmation, (3) in-process auth cache no TTL invalidation on key swap.
samir: Proposed long-term fixes: 
- Make rotation-runner wait for all pods to confirm secret pull (with exponential backoff).
- Ensure vault-agent uses leader election and coordinates lease renewals across sidecars.
- Add a short-lived cache-buster on key update so in-process caches drop stale keys (e.g., bump a cache-version header envvar).
- Add a preflight that checks every pod's env secret value after rotation before marking complete.
julie: Logged a support ticket to affected customers, told them we performed a restart and scheduled a follow-up. Will add postmortem once we have PRs.
maria: 403s dropped to baseline ~ 2 minutes after restart. Sending a rollback plan if issues recur.
kevin: I've opened PR #7824 for rotation-runner to add pod-confirmation checks. Samir, want to own the vault-agent leader-election change?
samir: Yep, I'll take it. Adding it to backlog and will schedule a canary for next week.
julie: Thanks all — updating ticket thread with repro and mitigation steps. :thumbsup:
